questions.question: What are some of the important advantages of Teflon tubing?
questions.idealAnswer: It is compatible with nearly every liquid, has a broad operating temperature range, low resistance to fluid flow and has a very long shelf and service life.

questions.question: What is the advantage of flexible Teflon hose over rubber hose?
questions.idealAnswer: Teflon hoses have better resistance to chemicals and a higher strength property at higher temperatures.

questions.question: Describe the method of classifying metal tube according to size.
questions.idealAnswer: Metal tubing is sized according to wall thickness and outside diameter. Outside diameter is measured in 1/16th inch increments.

questions.question: Describe the operation of quick disconnect couplings.
questions.idealAnswer: Each half has a valve that is held open when coupled and is spring-loaded closed when disconnected.

questions.question: Why are quick disconnect fittings used?
questions.idealAnswer: To provide a quick means to connect or disconnect a fluid line without loss of fluid or entrance of air into the system.

questions.question: Of what material are most low-pressure rigid fluid lines made?
questions.idealAnswer: 1100-1/2 hard or 3003-1/2 hard aluminum alloy tubing.

questions.question: What is the difference between the flare angle for aircraft and automotive fittings?
questions.idealAnswer: Aircraft fittings have a 37° flare angle and automotive fittings use 45°.

questions.question: What material should be selected for high-pressure rigid fluid lines?
questions.idealAnswer: Annealed or 1/4-hard corrosion-resistant steel.

questions.question: How tight should an MS flareless fitting be tightened?
questions.idealAnswer: Tighten the fitting by hand until it is snug, and then turn it with a wrench for 1/6-turn to 1/3-turn. Never turn it more than 1/3-turn with a wrench.

questions.question: What kind of rigid tubing can be flared with a double flare?
questions.idealAnswer: 5052-0 and 6061-T aluminum alloy tubing in sizes from 1/8-inch to 3/8-inch OD.

questions.question: What should be done to the end of a tube that is to be flared?
questions.idealAnswer: The cut end should be polished to remove any sharp edges that could cause the tubing to crack.

questions.question: If you fabricate a replacement for a flexible hose, what percentage of the total length must be added to allow for movement under pressure?
questions.idealAnswer: 5 to 8 percent.

questions.question: What pressure is used to proof-test a flexible hose assembly?
questions.idealAnswer: Typically, 1.5 times the recommended operating pressure of the hose.

questions.question: Why is it important to use a torque wrench when securing fluid hose and line fittings?
questions.idealAnswer: If the connection is too loose, it may leak. If the connection is too tight, it can cause the fitting to become damaged and fail.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using torque seal on a critical fitting after installation?
questions.idealAnswer: If a visual inspection reveals that the torque seal has broken, it is an indication that the fitting may have loosened.

questions.question: What are the two types of fluid lines commonly found in aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: Rigid metal lines and flexible hoses.

questions.question: When installing stainless steel tubing, what type of fittings should be used?
questions.idealAnswer: Stainless steel fittings.

questions.question: What is the function of the sleeve on a flared-tube fitting?
questions.idealAnswer: The nut fits over the sleeve and draws the sleeve and the tubing flare tightly against the male fitting to form the seal.

concepts.label: Nut fits draws tubing flare tightly against male form seal
terms: nut fits draws tubing flare tightly against male form seal

questions.question: Describe the two types of flares commonly used on aircraft tubing.
questions.idealAnswer: The single flare and the double flare.

questions.question: How can you determine if a fitting is an AN type rather than an AC type?
questions.idealAnswer: AN fittings have a shoulder between the flare cone and the end of the threads, AC fittings do not.

questions.question: What are the most significant differences between AN and AC fittings?
questions.idealAnswer: Sleeve length, thread pitch, and the shoulder between the threads and the flare cone on AN fittings.

questions.question: What are the names of the parts of a flareless tube fitting?
questions.idealAnswer: The nut and the ferrule or sleeve.

questions.question: How do you tell a flareless fitting from a flare-type fitting?
questions.idealAnswer: Flareless fittings don't have a flare cone and there is no space between the threads and the end of the fitting.

questions.question: What is the effect of over-tightening a flare type fitting?
questions.idealAnswer: The sealing surface may be damaged or the flare cut off.

questions.question: In addition to being securely clamped, what is an additional requirement for installing metal fuel, oil and hydraulic lines?
questions.idealAnswer: The lines must be electrically bonded to the structure.

questions.question: Describe the identification markings commonly found on flexible hoses.
questions.idealAnswer: A lay line, identification such as a Mil Spec number, the manufacturer's name or symbol, the hose size and a date code.

questions.question: How can you determine if a flexible hose has been correctly or incorrectly installed?
questions.idealAnswer: The lay line will be straight if the hose is properly installed. A twisted lay line indicates an incorrect installation.

conceptGroups.label: Twisted lay line indicates incorrect installation
acceptedTerms: twisted lay line indicates incorrect installation

questions.question: How are flexible hose sizes designated?
questions.idealAnswer: By the inside diameter, measured in 1/16th inch increments.

questions.question: What precautions must be observed when deburring the end of a tube after it is cut?
questions.idealAnswer: The wall thickness must not be reduced in size or fractured.

conceptGroups.label: Wall thickness not reduced size fractured

questions.question: What happens to the tube when a flareless fitting is overtightened?
questions.idealAnswer: The tube is weakened when the nut drives the cutting edge of the sleeve too deeply into the tube.

questions.question: What precautions should be taken when routing fluid lines adjacent to electrical wiring?
questions.idealAnswer: Route the fluid lines below the electrical wiring and maintain a clearance of at least six inches whenever possible. In no case should fluid lines and electrical wiring be closer than one-half inch. Ensure that both the wiring and the fluid lines are fastened to the aircraft structure by clamps or other methods that will maintain the separation.

questions.question: How often should flexible hoses be clamped in place?
questions.idealAnswer: Every 24 inches.

questions.question: Name considerations when installing flexible hose assemblies.
questions.idealAnswer: Slack, flexing, twisting, bending, clearance, and clamps.

questions.question: What are the three parts of a Military Standard (IVIS) tube fitting?
questions.idealAnswer: The body, the sleeve, and a nut.
